## Natural history notes

A large black swallowtail butterfly characterized by dark wings with pale greenish-blue scaling, rows of orange spots underneath, and short tail-like extensions on the hindwings. In Florida, it is found in hardwood hammocks, swamp edges, forest trails, gardens, parks, and wooded neighborhoods where spicebush, red bay, sassafras, or related host plants occur. Adults feed on nectar from flowering plants, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of these host plants and often hide in folded leaf shelters, with later instars resembling small snakes or bird droppings for protection.
